title.en: Hannah Weeps and Vows: The Birth of Samuel
title.zh: 哈拿泣而立願：撒母耳出生

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Hannah, barren and provoked yearly by her rival, weeps at Shiloh and vows her son to the LORD 'no razor shall come on his head'. Eli the priest takes her moving lips for drunkenness; she answers with dignity. Samuel — 'asked of God' — is born, weaned, and lent to the LORD all the days of his life.
summary.zh: 不育的哈拿年年受對頭激動，在示羅哭求並許願將子歸耶和華「不用剃刀剃他的頭」。祭司以利見其嘴唇動而以為醉；她尊嚴作答。撒母耳——「向神求來的」——出生斷奶，終身借與耶和華。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read as Rosh Hashanah haftarah.

passages.text: And she vowed a vow, and said: 'O LORD of hosts, if Thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of Thy handmaid, and remember me, and not forget Thy handmaid, but wilt give unto Thy handmaid a man-child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.'

Eli charged her: 'How long wilt thou be drunken? put away thy wine from thee.' Hannah answered: 'No, my lord; I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit... I have poured out my soul before the LORD.' 'Go in peace', he said, 'and the God of Israel grant thy petition'. When Samuel was born she named him 'because I have asked him of the LORD'; at weaning she brought him with sacrifices to Shiloh and left him with Eli, and 'the child ministered unto the LORD'. Paraphrase of 1 Samuel 1:14-28 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: My Heart Rejoiceth in the LORD: The Song of Hannah
title.zh: 我心因耶和華快樂：哈拿之歌

texts.period: Composed c. 10th-9th c. BCE (recorded 1 Samuel 2); principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Hannah's victory-poem on reversal — the barren bears seven, the full hire themselves out for bread; 'the bows of the mighty men are broken... He raiseth up the poor out of the dust... to make them inherit the throne of glory' — the theological key to the rise of the house of David, echoed in the Magnificat.
summary.zh: 哈拿的得勝詩論逆轉——不生育的生七子，飽足的反作佣人；「勇士的弓都已折斷……他從灰塵裡抬舉貧寒人……使他們與榮耀的寶座同分」——大衛家興起之神學鑰句，尊主頌所仿。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: The bows of the mighty men are broken; and they that stumbled are girded with strength. They that were full have hired out themselves for bread; and they that were hungry have ceased; while the barren hath borne seven; and she that hath many children hath languished. The LORD killeth, and maketh alive; He bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.

title.en: The Ark in the House of Dagon

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Israel carries the ark into battle 'as a talisman' and is routed; the ark is captured, Eli dies hearing the news, and the child's mother names him Ichabod — 'the glory is departed'. In Ashdod the Philistines set the ark beside Dagon: morning after morning the idol is found fallen, then broken before the ark, and tumors plague the cities until the ark is sent back with guilt-offerings of golden emerods and mice.
summary.zh: 以色列攜約櫃上陣「以為護符」而大敗；約櫃被擄，以利聞訊而死，產婦為子命名以迦博——「榮耀離開以色列了」。在亞實突，非利士人將約櫃置於大袞旁：日日清早神像撲倒，斷碎於櫃前，瘤災遍及諸城，直至以金痔金鼠為賠罪物送回。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And when they of Ashdod arose early on the morrow, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. And they took Dagon, and set him in his place again. And when they arose early on the morrow morning, behold, Dagon was fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold; only the trunk of Dagon was left to him.

The hand of the LORD was heavy on Ashdod and on its territory, destroying them with tumors; Ashdod, Gath, and Ekron in turn were smitten, and Ekron cried to send the ark away 'lest it bring us death'. The Philistine priests and diviners devised the return: a new cart with two milch kine, golden images of the tumors and of the mice 'that mar the land', and a trespass-offering. The kine lowed all the way to Beth-shemesh; the men of Beth-shemesh, who looked into the ark, were smitten — and the ark came to rest at Kirjath-jearim in the house of Abinadab. Paraphrase of 1 Samuel 5:6-6:21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Saul Seeks Asses and Finds a Kingdom

region.en: Ramah and Mizpah, land of Benjamin
region.zh: 拉瑪與米斯巴，便雅憫地

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Kish's son Saul, taller by a head than any in Israel, goes searching for strayed asses and arrives at Samuel's town by providence. Samuel, told by God the day before, seats him above the guests, pours oil on his head, and predicts the signs on his road home. The spirit comes on him among the prophets; at Mizpah he is drawn by lot, hiding among the baggage, and acclaimed king: 'God save the king!'
summary.zh: 便雅憫人基士之子掃羅，身量比眾民高過一頭，為尋失驢而至撒母耳之城，實為天意。撒母耳前夜得神諭，請他坐客位之上，以膏油澆其頭，並預言歸途諸兆。靈感動他在先知中說話；米斯巴掣籤被指出，藏於器械中，眾民呼喊「願王萬歲！」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said: 'Is it not because the LORD hath anointed thee to be prince over His inheritance? ... And the spirit of the LORD will come mightily upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 10:1, 6 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: To Obey Is Better Than Sacrifice: Saul and Agag
title.zh: 聽命勝於獻祭：掃羅與亞甲

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Saul is sent to destroy Amalek utterly but spares Agag and the best of the flocks 'to sacrifice'. Samuel's rebirth of the prophetic word — 'Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt-offerings... Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice' — ends Saul's dynasty: 'thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD hath rejected thee'. Samuel hews Agag in pieces before the LORD at Gilgal and mourns for Saul 'unto his dying day'.
summary.zh: 掃羅奉命滅盡亞瑪力人，卻存留亞甲與上好的牛羊「要獻與耶和華」。撒母耳重申預言之道——「耶和華喜悅燔祭和平安祭，豈如喜悅人聽從他的話呢……聽命勝於獻祭」——掃羅王朝至此終結：「你既厭棄耶和華的命令，耶和華也厭棄你」。撒母耳在吉甲耶和華面前將亞甲斬為碎片，為掃羅悲傷「直到死的日子」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Amalek becomes the recurring symbol of genocidal enmity in Jewish memory; record states text only.

passages.text: And Samuel said: 'Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt-offerings and sacrifices, as in hearkening to the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams. For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, He hath also rejected thee from being king.'

title.en: The Oil of Bethlehem: David Chosen from the Fields
title.zh: 伯利恆的膏油：田間被選的大衛

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Sent to Bethlehem with a heifer to anoint a son of Jesse, Samuel passes seven sons before the LORD and is corrected: 'the LORD seeth not as man seeth... the LORD looketh on the heart'. David, the youngest, is fetched from the sheep; 'and the spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward'. The same chapter has the distressed Saul's servants call for a man 'skilful in playing a harp' — David's double call: oil and harp.
summary.zh: 撒母耳持牛犢往伯利恆膏耶西之子，七子一一經過皆非；神糾正：「耶和華不像人看人……人是看外貌，耶和華是看內心。」幼子大衛自羊圈中被召；「從那日起，耶和華的靈就感動大衛」。同章記受攪擾的掃羅之僕薦「善於彈琴」者——大衛的雙重蒙召：膏油與琴。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said: 'Arise, anoint him; for this is he.' Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren; and the spirit of the LORD came mightily upon David from that day forward.

title.en: Five Smooth Stones: David and Goliath
title.zh: 五塊光滑石子：大衛與歌利亞

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: For forty days the giant of Gath defies Israel's ranks. The shepherd-boy David, sent with provisions, hears the taunt and volunteers: 'The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion... He will deliver me'. He refuses Saul's armour, chooses five smooth stones from the brook, fells Goliath with one stone, and cuts off his head with the giant's own sword — while the Philistine army flees.
summary.zh: 四十日之久，迦特巨人向以色列軍陣罵陣。送糧的牧童大衛聞言自薦：「耶和華救我脫離獅子和熊的爪，也必救我脫離這非利士人的手。」他拒絕掃羅的戰衣，自溪中揀五塊光滑石子，一石擊倒歌利亞，以巨人自己的刀割其首——非利士全軍潰逃。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Folk-epic of the small against the giant; cross-tradition giant-slayer cluster.

passages.text: And David said unto the Philistine: 'Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast taunted.' ... And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it, and smote the Philistine in his forehead; and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell upon his face to the earth.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 17:45, 49 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: Jonathan's Soul Was Knit to David
title.zh: 約拿單的心與大衛深相契合

region.en: Gibeah of Saul, land of Benjamin
region.zh: 掃羅的基比亞，便雅憫地

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The prince strips himself of robe, armour, sword, and bow and gives them to David — 'and it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul'. Saul hurls his spear; Jonathan shields David with the sign of the missing arrows at the field of stones: 'hasten thou, be not stayed'.
summary.zh: 王子將外袍、戰衣、刀、弓、腰帶都給了大衛——「大衛與掃羅說完了話，約拿單的心與大衛的心深相契合，約拿單愛他如同愛自己的性命」。掃羅掄槍刺他；約拿單在田野以射箭之號護衛大衛：「你快跑吧，不要停留。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Jonathan caused David to swear again, for the love that he had to him; for he loved him as he loved his own soul. ... And Jonathan said unto David: 'The LORD be with thee, as He hath been with my father.' ... And Jonathan gave his weapons unto his lad, and said unto his lad: 'Go, carry them to the city.' ... As soon as the lad was gone, David arose out of a place toward the south, and fell on his face to the ground, and bowed himself three times; and they kissed one another, and wept one with another, until David exceeded.

title.en: The Massacre at Nob: Doeg the Edomite

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Fleeing, David begs the shewbread from Ahimelech the priest 'as if common' and takes Goliath's sword. Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, sees and reports. Saul orders the priests slain; his servants refuse, and Doeg 'turned and fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons'. Abiathar alone escapes to David, bringing the ephod — and David's guilt: 'I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father's house.'
summary.zh: 逃亡的大衛向祭司亞希米勒求「平常的」陳設餅，並取歌利亞的刀。掃羅的司牧長以東人多益目擊而告發。掃羅命殺祭司；僕人不從，多益「伸刀殺了那日八十五人」。唯亞比亞他逃奔大衛，攜以弗得同來——大衛自認其咎：「你父的全家喪命，都是因我的緣故。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the king said to Doeg: 'Turn thou, and fall upon the priests.' And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod. And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen and asses and sheep, with the edge of the sword.

title.en: Nabal the Fool and Abigail's Beautiful Judgment
title.zh: 拿八愚頑與亞比該的美麗判斷

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Rich Nabal — 'the fool' — repulses David's men who had guarded his shearers. David moves to slaughter the house; Abigail intercepts him with two hundred loaves and wine and a speech so wise he blesses 'the God of Israel... who sent thee this day to meet me': 'blessed be thy counsel, and blessed be thou'. Nabal's heart dies within him; ten days later 'the LORD smote Nabal, that he died', and David takes Abigail to wife.
summary.zh: 富有的拿八——「愚頑人」——拒絕曾護其剪羊毛者的大衛之僕。大衛率眾欲滅其家；亞比該攜二百餅與酒迎之，言辭明智，大衛頌「以色列的神……今日打發你迎接我」是稱頌：「你的見識值得稱讚，你也當得稱讚」。拿八魂不附體；十日後「耶和華擊打拿八，他就死了」，大衛娶亞比該。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then Abigail made haste, and took two hundred loaves, and two bottles of wine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched corn, and an hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses. And she said unto her servants: 'Go on before me; behold, I come after you.' ... And she fell at his feet, and said: 'Upon me, my lord, upon me let this iniquity be; and let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thine ears.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 25:18-19, 24 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: The Woman of Endor Raises Samuel
title.zh: 隱多珥的女巫召撒母耳

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The night before Gilboa, with the LORD silent 'by dreams, or by Urim, or by prophets', a disguised Saul — who had himself purged the mediums — seeks the woman of Endor. She conjures 'a god' and sees 'gods ascending out of the earth'; Samuel comes up as an old man wrapped in a robe and pronounces the doom: 'To-morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me.' Saul falls straightway to the ground, full length, faint with fasting.
summary.zh: 基利波戰前之夜，耶和華「藉夢、或烏陵、或先知」都不回答；曾親自剪除交鬼之人的掃羅喬裝求助於隱多珥的女人。她招「一個神」上來，見「有神從地裡上來」；撒母耳如披衣的老人出現，宣告定命：「明日你和你的眾子必與我在一處。」掃羅立刻仆倒在地，身體僵直，因一夜沒有喫飯。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Necromancy is forbidden by Torah (Deut 18); the narrative presents the episode's ambiguity.

passages.text: And Samuel said to Saul: 'Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up?' And Saul answered: 'I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me.' And Samuel said: 'Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the LORD is departed from thee... And tomorrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me.'

title.en: Fallen on Gilboa: Saul's Last Day
title.zh: 基利波山之傾覆：掃羅末日

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The battle goes against Israel; the archers overtake the king and his three sons die. Wounded by the archers, Saul begs his armour-bearer to slay him, then falls on his own sword. The Philistines fasten his body on the wall of Beth-shan; the men of Jabesh-gilead, remembering his first deed as king, rescue the bodies by night and burn and bury them. David's lament — 'How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!' — and his eulogy of Jonathan crown the king he replaced.
summary.zh: 戰事不利，弓箭手追上王，三子皆亡。掃羅中箭重傷，求拿兵器者刺死不從，遂自伏刀上。非利士人將其屍釘在伯珊城牆；基列雅比人念其首位救民之功，夜間取回屍身焚化而葬。大衛作哀歌——「大英雄何竟死亡！約拿單的弓箭非流敵人的血不退縮」——尊榮他所取代的王。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armour-bearer, and all his men, that same day together. ... And they took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh, and burnt their bones there, and buried them under the terebinth in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Samuel 31:6, 12-13 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

passages.text: An Amalekite brings the news and claims to have given the death-stroke; David orders him slain for 'saying he had destroyed the LORD's anointed'. Then David laments from the Book of Jashar: 'The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places; how are the mighty fallen... ye mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew'. For Jonathan: 'I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan; very pleasant hast thou been unto me... How are the mighty fallen!' Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 1:1-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: David Dances Before the Ark of the LORD
title.zh: 大衛在耶和華的約櫃前踴躍跳舞

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Bringing the ark up from Kirjath-jearim on a new cart, Uzzah touches it to steady it and dies 'beside the ark of God'. David fears the LORD's presence and defers the journey; three months later it is carried properly, with sacrifices every six paces. The king leaps and dances before the ark in a linen ephod — Michal's scorn at 'the base fellow exposing himself' earns her childlessness.
summary.zh: 自基列耶琳以新車運櫃，烏撒扶櫃而立斃「在神的約櫃旁」。大衛懼耶和華之臨，中止行程；三月後以正法抬行，每六步獻祭。君王穿細麻布以弗得在櫃前踴躍跳舞——米甲譏其「露體」如愚妄人，因而無子到死。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And it was so, that, when they that bore the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling. And David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was girded with a linen ephod. So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the horn.

title.en: Thou Art the Man: Nathan's Parable of the Ewe Lamb
title.zh: 你就是那人：拿單的羊羔寓言

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The king sees Bathsheba bathing, takes her, and has Uriah — loyal soldier of the front lines — killed by his own signed orders 'with the sword of the children of Ammon'. Nathan tells the rich man who took the poor man's one ewe lamb; David's 'the man shall surely die' turns on himself: 'Thou art the man.' The child of the union dies; Solomon is born and 'the LORD loved him'.
summary.zh: 王見拔示巴沐浴而取之，又以其親筆密令使忠誠前線的烏利亞「死在亞捫人的刀下」。拿單以富戶奪貧者唯一羊羔設喻；大衛怒曰「行這事的人該死」，反及其身：「你就是那人。」所生之子死；所羅門生，「耶和華也喜愛他」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Nathan said to David: 'Thou art the man. Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel: I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul... wherefore hast thou despised the word of the LORD, to do that which is evil in My sight?'

The parable: a rich man with many flocks takes a poor neighbour's 'one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and reared... and it lay in his bosom'. David's anger 'was greatly kindled' and he passed the death sentence; Nathan's sentence-echo exposed the king. David confessed 'I have sinned against the LORD'; the penalty fell on the child, who died on the seventh day — while David, having fasted, rose and washed and ate, saying 'he shall not come back to me, but I shall go to him'. Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 12:1-24 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Absalom in the Oak: The Revolt and the King's Grief
title.zh: 橡樹間的押沙龍：叛亂與王之哀哭

region.en: Forest of Ephraim, east of the Jordan

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Absalom steals hearts at the gate — 'Thy matters are good... oh that I were judge in the land!' — and has himself acclaimed king at Hebron. David flees over Kidron weeping, his head covered; Absalom's hair catches in the terebinth as his mule passes under, and Joab's darts finish him despite David's own command. The king's cry to the messenger echoes down the ages: 'O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee.'
summary.zh: 押沙龍在城門偷取民心——「你的事有情有理……恨不得我作國中的士師！」——於希伯崙自立為王。大衛蒙頭上基訓逃亡哭泣；押沙龍騎騾經過橡樹下，頭髮被樹枝繞住，約押的槍了結他——雖王曾嚴令存其性命。王對報信者的哭聲流傳千古：「押沙龍，我兒，我兒！恨不得我替你死。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the man said unto Joab: 'Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in a terebinth.' ... And Joab took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the terebinth. ... And Absalom took, and cast him into a great pit in the forest, and raised a very great heap of stones over him.

David sat between the two gates while the watchman announced the victory. When he heard the son was dead he went up to the chamber over the gate and wept: 'O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!' Joab rebuked the shamed army — 'thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends' — and the king arose and sat in the gate. Paraphrase of 2 Samuel 18:24-33; 19:1-8 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
